mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted, {أمرا من عندنَا}: أمرا is accusative, according to al-Akhfash, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the sense of آمرين ("commanding"). Al-Mubarrad said it is in the position of a maṣdar (verbal noun), as though He said "We sent it down with a sending down". Al-Jarmī said it is a ḥāl from an indefinite noun, namely أمر حكيم; that is good since the indefinite noun has been described, and he allowed هذا رجل مقبلا. Al-Zajjāj said it is a maṣdar, as though He said يُفرق فرقا, so it is in the sense of فرق. It has also been said that يفرق is in the sense of يؤمر ("is commanded"), so it is again a maṣdar governed by what precedes it.

[Translator's note: the source has «امرين», evidently for «آمرين».]

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying {رَحْمَة من رَبك}: al-Akhfash said رحمة is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Farrāʾ said it is the object of مرسلين, making the mercy the Prophet, upon him be peace. Al-Zajjāj said رحمة is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of mercy", with the object of مرسلين omitted. It has also been said that it is a badal (substitute) for أمر; and it has been said that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying {أَنى لَهُم الذكرى}: الذكرى is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أنّى the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:15-15.t:
His saying {قَلِيلا}: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an omitted ẓarf (adverbial), its implied form being "a little removal" or "a little time".

His saying {رب السَّمَاوَات}: whoever put it in the nominative made it a naʿt of السميع, or (nominative) by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject); whoever put it in the genitive made it a badal (substitute) for ربك.

[Translator's note: رب السماوات is in āya 7, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {يَوْم نبطش}: يوم is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "remember, O Muhammad, the day We strike".

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying {أَن أَدّوا إِلَيّ}: أن is in the accusative position by omission of the preposition, i.e. "with (the message) that: deliver to me"; and عباد الله is accusative, governed by أدّوا. It has also been said that it is a vocative with a muḍāf; if you put عباد in the accusative as a vocative, the object of أدّوا is omitted, i.e. "deliver to me your affair, O servants of Allah".

mekki-muskil:19-19.t: His saying {وَأَن لَا تعلوا}: أن is conjoined to the first أن, in the accusative position.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying {أَن ترجمون}: أن is in the accusative position by omission of the preposition, i.e. "from (من) that you stone me", meaning "revile me".

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying {فَدَعَا ربه أَن هَؤُلَاءِ}: أنّ is in the accusative position, governed by دعا. Whoever gave it kasra did so by an implied saying, i.e. "and he said: these…".

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying {واترك الْبَحْر رهوا}: رهوا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the sense of "still", so that they would get into it and not shy away from it; one says عيش راهٍ, i.e. a life that is still and at ease. It has also been said that الرهو is "parted", i.e. leave it as it is, parted, path upon path, so that they get into it.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying {كم تركُوا}: كم is in the accusative position, governed by تركوا.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t:
His saying {كَذَلِك وأورثناها}: the kāf is in the nominative position as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the matter is thus". It has also been said that it is in the accusative position, on the implied form "We do a doing like that to whomever We wish to destroy".

[Translator's note: the source has «تفعل», evidently for «نفعل».]

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying {إِلَّا موتتنا}: موتتنا is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of مَا, because إن is in the sense of مَا; so the implied form is "it is nothing but our first death".

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying {وَالَّذين من قبلهم}: الذين is in the nominative position, conjoined to قوم تبّع, or as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with what follows it as the khabar (predicate); or it is in the accusative position by an implied verb indicated by أهلكناهم.

mekki-muskil:40-40.t: His saying إن يوم الفصل: يوم is the ism (noun) of إنّ, and its khabar (predicate) is ميقاتهم. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ allowed ميقاتَهم to be accusative by إنّ, making يوم الفصل an adverb (ẓarf) for the appointed time, in the position of the khabar of إنّ, i.e. "their appointed time is on the Day of Decision".

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {يَوْم لَا يُغني}: it is a badal (substitute) for the first يوم.

mekki-muskil:42-42.t: His saying {إِلَّا من رحم الله}: من is in the nominative position as a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in ينصرون, its implied form being "none will be helped except whom Allah has shown mercy". It has also been said that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being "except whom Allah has shown mercy: he will be pardoned". It has also been said that it is a badal for the first مولى, the implied form being "the day when none avails except whom Allah has shown mercy", i.e. none will intercede except whom Allah has shown mercy. This is a proof of the permissibility of intercession by believers for sinful believers, by the permission of Allah the Exalted. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said it is in the accusative position as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).

mekki-muskil:49-49.t: His saying {ذُقْ إِنَّك}: whoever read it with kasra on إنّ made it the beginning of a new sentence, meaning: "you used to say this of yourself in the world, and it used to be said to you" — and he is Abū Jahl, may Allah curse him. It has also been said that its meaning with kasra is an ironic allusion to him, meaning: "you are the humiliated and disgraced one now, contrary to what you used to say and what used to be said to you in the world." Whoever gave it fatḥa did so on the implied omission of the prepositional lām, i.e. "because you…" or "for (بأنك) you are the one to whom that used to be said in the world and who used to say it of himself". It is related that he used to say: "I am the mightiest and best-defended of the people of the valley." The kasra indicates that.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying {مُتَقَابلين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in يلبسون.

mekki-muskil:54-54.t: His saying {كَذَلِك}: the kāf is in the nominative position, i.e. "the matter is thus". It has also been said that it is in the accusative position as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "(He) does to the God-fearing a doing like that".

mekki-muskil:55-55.t: His saying {يدعونَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in زوجناهم; likewise آمنين, and likewise لا يذوقون.

mekki-muskil:56-56.t: His saying {إِلَّا الموتة}: a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). It has also been said that إلا is in the sense of بعد ("after"), and it has been said in the sense of سوى ("other than"). The first is better.

mekki-muskil:57-57.t: His saying {فضلا من رَبك}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) governed by يدعون فيها. It has also been said that what governs it is ووقاهم, and it has been said that what governs it is آمنين.
